resources.string:
Cassini: more to discover on every card

Plan your night

Info cards now show live facts and what\'s next. The Moon card shows its phase, how much is lit and its age, and the Moon, planet and meteor shower cards each have an Upcoming section so you know when to look.

Satellites

Look for the International Space Station (ISS) and Tiangong (CSS) on the map. Switch on the Satellites layer, then tap one to see its next visible passes. Turn on Satellite passes under Settings → Notifications to be told before a pass begins. The orbit data downloads the first time you use the layer, which can take a few minutes.

A new graphics engine (beta)

There is a new graphics engine, available as a beta: a more realistic daytime and twilight sky, and clearer labels, with a subtle underline on objects that have an info card. It is off by default. To try it, choose Enhanced under Settings → Appearance → Graphics engine, and switch back to Classic any time. We would love to hear how it works on your phone.

Also new

  • Brighter or dimmer grid: choose how bright the grid lines are, and see more grid labels.
  • Smaller Moon widget: the Moon phase widget now comes in a compact 1x1 size.
  • Better search: find asterisms such as the Big Dipper, and Earth.

And this is just the start...

We have many long asked-for features coming very soon.

About the release name

Cassini was the NASA/ESA/ASI spacecraft that orbited Saturn from 2004 to 2017, studying its rings and moons and delivering the Huygens probe to the surface of Titan.

resources.string:
Sky Map comes to iPhone

This is the first iPhone release of Sky Map. It began at Google in 2009 as Google Sky Map, and has been an independent open-source project for well over a decade. Hold your iPhone up and the sky follows your view.

And this is just the start...

More is on the way. Tell us what you would like from the Support screen.
